note: Prince of Persia, DOS 1.0. Which resource of which DAT is what, as the game loads them (SDLPoP seg000.c load_*; resource ids and palette rows from the load_chtab_from_file / load_sprites_from_file calls). Paths relative to this spec. Palette row r = the chtab's 16 colours land in VGA registers r*16..r*16+15 and its pixels are written as r*16+colour.

flameSwordPotion.note: flames 1-9, sword on the floor 10-11, potions 12-15, bubbles 16-22, bubble mask 23 (chtab 1)

guard.note: GUARD.DAT has no palette resource; the game opens GUARD2.DAT (dungeon) or GUARD1.DAT (palace) underneath it for resource 750, and recolours the set per guard from guardPalettes (chtab 5)

dungeon.note: dungeon tiles (chtab 6); optional graphics 1200+n replace image n (load_more_opt_graf)

titleFrame.note: story frame and texts; colour 14 is set by the game (dark blue / dark red)

titlePictures.note: title screen, 'presents', 'a game by', logo, 'Jordan Mechner'

princessRoom.note: chtab 8, image 1 is the whole room background

levels.note: level n is resource 2000+n; 0 demo, 1-13 the game, 14 the vizier, 15 copy protection

instruments.note: the AdLib instrument table the MIDI driver plays through: a count byte and then 16 bytes an instrument (blockLow, blockHigh, feedback/connection, 2x {multiple, level, attackDecay, sustainRelease, waveform}, percussion, 2 unused) — SDLPoP midi.c init_midi, types.h instrument_type. MIDI channel n starts on instrument n, a program change moves it.

sounds.note: digiLayout: the digitised header of 1.0/1.1 (rate, count, unknown, sampleSize) vs 1.3/1.4 (rate, sampleSize, count, unknown, unknown2); sound n is resource 10000+n in every sound DAT; the game opens IBM_SND (speaker), DIGISND (digitised) and MIDISND (AdLib) and takes the first that has it. Names are ours, after doc/internals_sounds.csv of SDLPoP.

guardPalettes.note: 7 guard colours x 16 VGA colours x rgb (6-bit); colour c of a guard = bytes 48*(c-1).. (seg003.c set_chtab_palette)

unknown.note: not referenced by SDLPoP; kept as base64 until identified. Resource 1 was here too until it was identified as the AdLib instrument table (sounds.instruments)

exe.note: Program data of the executable the game logic runs on: the animation sequences and the frame tables. Found by their first bytes (SDLPoP seqtbl.c / seg006.c give the content); 'entries' x 'stride' bytes follow. seqOffsets sit at data:1888 of the data segment whose base is where the sequence table (data:196E) was found.

seqOffsets.note: word per SEQ id; entry 0 is unused (0xB000 in the file)
